new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed and it was fully opened and confirmed silent. Spot-checks of the companion sources already held by the project for this glottocode: Loukotka 1968 (djvu text) has a general convention 'Stress: à é í ó ú' in its Introduction (line 1760, p. 36) but says nothing about stress in the Natú entry (p. 88), and its Natú forms carry only one such mark (barí, tobacco) plus length colons, so no placement rule can be read off; Lima Neto & Nunes 2022 pp. 414-415 (the text layer) list the 'acentos tônicos' (acute, circumflex, macron, tilde) purely as graphemes of the Xokó/Natú transcriptions with no statement of where stress falls; Loukotka 1955 and Meader 1978 have no accent/stress…
